Bias and linearity of a numeric LLM pipeline against a reference

Source: R/agreement.R
msa_bias.Rd

Compares parsed numeric values with reference values per item: mean bias with a t-based confidence interval overall and per prompt-model combination, and a linearity check (does the bias depend on the magnitude of the reference?) by regressing the bias on the reference.

Usage

msa_bias(runs, reference, level = 0.95)

Arguments

runs

An msa_runs object with numeric values.

reference

A named numeric vector keyed by item_id, a data.frame with columns item_id and reference, or a column name in runs. Each item has at most one distinct readable reference; conflicting references are errors. A known value beside missing entries supplies that item's reference. Factor labels are read as numbers.

level

Finite numeric confidence level strictly between zero and one.

Value

An object of class msa_bias, with:

overall

Named numeric vector n, bias, sd, lower, upper, p_value, n_excluded.

by_condition

The same quantities per observed prompt-model combination. With no valid pair all estimates are NA.

linearity

Handbook intercept, slope, slope_p_value, r_squared (proportion), t_intercept, t_slope, df, t_quantile.

linearity_item_means

Unweighted item-mean intercept, slope, r_squared, t_intercept, t_slope, df.

linearity_band

Data frame reference, fit, lower, upper, at each distinct reference value; empty when the band is undefined.

linearity_in_band

Logical scalar: zero lies in the entire handbook band, or NA when undefined.

linearity_verdict

"acceptable" when the entire band contains zero, "unacceptable" otherwise, or NA_character_ when undefined.

linearity_note

Methods, both degrees of freedom, dependence limitation and any reason for undefined linearity.

level, n_items

Confidence level and count of items with valid pairs.

Details

Missing, NaN and unparseable responses or references are excluded and counted once per row in n_excluded. Infinite inputs and overflow of the response minus reference are errors. All observed prompt-model conditions remain in the output, even with no valid pairs. If there are no valid pairs overall, the call fails with an explanatory error.

The bias interval and p-value use the one-sample t calculation with n - 1 degrees of freedom. One valid pair gives its bias but no inference. Numerically constant deviations give a point interval and an undefined p-value, with a message; the measured SD is retained. Constancy means a zero standard error, or a standard error smaller than ten times machine precision times the absolute mean.

The handbook regression uses all valid single deviations (N - 2 degrees of freedom, or gm - 2 in a balanced design). The additional regression uses unweighted item means (g - 2 degrees of freedom). Items with the same reference value remain distinct. Unequal replicate counts thus give different weighting in the two regressions. Replicates of the same item may be correlated, so the handbook calculation can overstate the information. The object and report describe this limitation.

The handbook confidence band for the mean bias determines the linearity verdict. Zero must lie in the band throughout the closed observed reference range, including between displayed reference values; touching the boundary counts as inclusion. This is not a prediction interval. A single reference value leaves linearity undefined without preventing bias estimation. Without residual degrees of freedom, coefficients are retained but inference and the band are undefined. Numerically constant targets have undefined R-squared. A residual norm no larger than ten times machine precision times the centered target norm is treated as zero: t and p are undefined and the band collapses onto the fitted line. These cases produce messages and NA, never NaN.

Examples

msa_bias(ic50_demo, reference = "reference")
#> Bias against reference (40 items, 2152 values)
#>   Excluded response-reference pairs: 8
#>   mean bias 0.0110  [95 % CI 0.0030, 0.0190]  sd 0.1885  p = 0.00682
#>  prompt_id model_id   n    bias     sd   lower   upper  p_value n_excluded
#>     direct  model-a 239 -0.0061 0.1468 -0.0248  0.0126    0.519          1
#>   stepwise  model-a 240  0.0835 0.1530  0.0640  0.1029 2.87e-15          0
#>      table  model-a 240 -0.0502 0.1429 -0.0684 -0.0320 1.31e-07          0
#>     direct  model-b 239 -0.1267 0.1338 -0.1438 -0.1097 4.77e-35          1
#>   stepwise  model-b 239 -0.0505 0.1495 -0.0696 -0.0315 3.78e-07          1
#>      table  model-b 238 -0.1819 0.1404 -0.1998 -0.1639 9.61e-53          2
#>     direct  model-c 239  0.1432 0.1432  0.1250  0.1615  8.1e-38          1
#>   stepwise  model-c 239  0.2206 0.1411  0.2026  0.2386 5.02e-66          1
#>      table  model-c 239  0.0663 0.1453  0.0478  0.0848 1.87e-11          1
#>   Handbook linearity: bias = 0.0278 + -0.0092 * reference (slope p = 0.0268)
#>     R-squared 0.0023; t intercept 3.234; t slope -2.215; df 2150; t quantile 1.9611
#>   Item means: bias = 0.0278 + -0.0092 * reference; R-squared 0.0274; t intercept 1.510; t slope -1.034; df 38
#>   Handbook linearity verdict: unacceptable
#> The handbook regression uses all valid single deviations (df = 2150; gm - 2 in a balanced design); the regression on unweighted item means uses df = 38 (g - 2). Replicates of the same item may be correlated and are not independent. The handbook confidence band determines the linearity verdict.
